items.slide_topic: Splash M1237: 'How models are made' / 'nobody fully understands the inside' beat (AI is grown, not built)
items.dek: As my friend and co-founder Chris Olah is fond of saying, generative AI systems are grown more than they are built—their internal mechanisms are “emergent” rather than directly designed. It’s a bit like growing a plant or a bacterial colony: we set the high-level conditions that direct and shape growth, but the exact structure which emerges is unpredictable and difficult to understand or explain.
items.author: Dario Amodei
items.caption: Dario Amodei, 'The Urgency of Interpretability' (essay, April 2025): AI systems are 'grown more than they are built'.
items.notes: Verbatim from the loaded essay page (footnote marker removed). The page header reads only 'April 2025'; the day 2025-04-24 is an inference from the TechCrunch article dated April 24, 2025 that says Amodei 'published an essay Thursday'. Amodei credits the line to co-founder Chris Olah ('is fond of saying'), so attribute it that way. Use this essay wording, not TechCrunch's paraphrase.

items.slide_topic: Splash M1237: 'How models are made' / 'nobody fully understands the inside' beat (secondary press coverage)
items.headline: Anthropic CEO wants to open the black box of AI models by 2027
items.dek: In the essay, Amodei notes that Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah says that AI models are “grown more than they are built.” In other words, AI researchers have found ways to improve AI model intelligence, but they don’t quite know why.
items.author: Maxwell Zeff
items.caption: TechCrunch, April 24, 2025: the article's paragraph summarising the 'grown more than they are built' line.
items.notes: Headline and byline verbatim from the loaded page (4:28 PM PDT, April 24, 2025). The quoted line is TechCrunch's paraphrase ('AI models are' rather than the essay's 'generative AI systems are'), so do not quote it as Amodei's exact words. Good as a credible-outlet citation card. The essay itself says the goal was 'interpretability can reliably detect most model problems' by 2027, which TechCrunch paraphrases differently.

items.slide_topic: Splash M1237: 'How models are made' (Chris Olah's own phrasing, reported in press)
items.dek: We don’t program AI, we grow it
items.author: Caiwei Chen
items.caption: Chris Olah, quoted by The Daily Dot (Nov 14, 2024) from his Lex Fridman podcast interview: 'We don’t program AI, we grow it.'
items.notes: Quote verified verbatim in the page text of the loaded article ('“We don’t program AI, we grow it,” Olah said'). Its context is the Lex Fridman interview, which I did not check against a transcript, so cite it as 'as reported by The Daily Dot'. WARNING: the article's headline is about 'Trump neurons' in the CLIP model. Do not show that headline or any political figure name on the slide; use only the quote and the attribution.

facts.claim: Dario Amodei's essay says generative AI systems are “grown more than they are built—their internal mechanisms are ‘emergent’ rather than directly designed.”
facts.source: Dario Amodei, 'The Urgency of Interpretability' (essay page dated 'April 2025'; day inferred as 2025-04-24)

facts.claim: Amodei credits the 'grown more than they are built' line to co-founder Chris Olah: “As my friend and co-founder Chris Olah is fond of saying…”

“It’s a bit like growing a plant or a bacterial colony: we set the high-level conditions that direct and shape growth, but the exact structure which emerges is unpredictable and difficult to understand or explain.”

“People outside the field are often surprised and alarmed to learn that we do not understand how our own AI creations work. They are right to be concerned: this lack of understanding is essentially unprecedented in the history of technology.”
Amodei: “I am very concerned about deploying such systems without a better handle on interpretability.”
Amodei's essay sets Anthropic a goal of getting to “interpretability can reliably detect most model problems” by 2027.
Amodei: “on its current trajectory I would bet strongly in favor of interpretability reaching this point within 5-10 years” (this point = a “true ‘MRI for AI’”).
Chris Olah: “We don’t program AI, we grow it.”
facts.source: The Daily Dot (Caiwei Chen), reporting Olah's Lex Fridman podcast interview
